Contraindicated - not for use in known or suspected pregnancy

No specific adjustment for single-dose EC; caution in severe impairment

summary: Ulipristal acetate is a selective progesterone receptor modulator. As a single 30 mg dose (ella) it is an emergency contraceptive effective up to 120 hours after unprotected intercourse, acting mainly by delaying or inhibiting ovulation. At a 5 mg daily dose (Esmya, EU - not FDA approved for this) it was used to treat uterine fibroids, but that indication carries restrictions due to rare serious liver injury. It is contraindicated in established pregnancy.
indications: Emergency contraception - prevention of pregnancy after unprotected intercourse or suspected contraceptive failure (single 30 mg dose, ella)
(EU only, restricted) Intermittent or pre-operative treatment of moderate-to-severe symptoms of uterine fibroids (5 mg daily, Esmya)

dosage.d: One 30 mg tablet as a single dose
dosage.t: As soon as possible, within 120 hours (5 days) of unprotected intercourse
dosage.n: Repeat the dose if vomiting occurs within 3 hours; may be taken at any point in the cycle

dosage.t: In treatment courses of up to 3 months, with liver monitoring
dosage.n: NOT FDA-approved for fibroids; EU use restricted to selected patients with liver function monitoring

admin: Emergency contraception: take one tablet as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse, with or without food
If vomiting occurs within 3 hours, consider repeating the dose
After ella, initiate or resume hormonal contraception no sooner than 5 days later and use a reliable barrier method until the next period
Fibroid use (EU): perform liver function tests before, during, and after treatment courses
moa: Ulipristal acetate binds the progesterone receptor as an agonist/antagonist (SPRM). For emergency contraception, taken just before ovulation it postpones follicular rupture, so the primary mechanism is inhibition or delay of ovulation; endometrial alterations that may impair implantation can also contribute. For fibroids, it directly suppresses endometrial and fibroid cell proliferation and reduces bleeding.

absolute: (Fibroid use) underlying hepatic disorder / liver impairment
relative: Severe asthma insufficiently controlled by oral glucocorticoids
Repeated use within the same menstrual cycle (EC not intended for routine/repeat use)

preg: Contraindicated in known or suspected pregnancy. Ulipristal is not indicated to terminate an existing pregnancy. Women who become pregnant or have lower abdominal pain after use should be evaluated for ectopic pregnancy.
lact: For single-dose emergency contraception, breastfeeding is not recommended for about 1 week after intake (express and discard milk per product information). For fibroid (chronic) use, breastfeeding should be avoided.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is recommended for single-dose emergency contraception; use with caution in severe renal impairment as it has not been specifically studied.
hepatic: Use is not recommended in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment for single-dose EC. For the EU fibroid indication, liver function monitoring is mandated and the product is restricted because of rare serious hepatic injury.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's Wort) - reduce ulipristal effectiveness; avoid
Progestin-containing contraceptives / progestins (including levonorgestrel) - may reduce ulipristal's ability to delay ovulation; avoid concurrent intake
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole) - increase ulipristal exposure
Drugs that increase gastric pH may reduce absorption
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction for single-dose use
interactions.diagnostics: Pregnancy test if menses delayed >1 week or pregnancy suspected; liver function tests for fibroid use

serious: (Fibroid/chronic use) serious hepatic injury including rare liver failure
emergency: Severe lower abdominal pain (possible ectopic pregnancy)
Signs of acute liver injury during chronic fibroid use (jaundice, severe fatigue, dark urine)

monitoring: Emergency contraception: no routine monitoring; confirm pregnancy if menses is delayed by more than 1 week
Evaluate for ectopic pregnancy if pregnancy occurs or there is lower abdominal pain
Fibroid use (EU): liver function tests before, during, and after treatment courses
counsel: Take the emergency contraceptive tablet as soon as possible - sooner is more effective (up to 5 days)
Repeat the dose if you vomit within 3 hours
Your next period may come earlier or later than expected; if it is more than a week late, do a pregnancy test
Use a barrier method (condoms) until your next period; resume/start hormonal birth control no sooner than 5 days after
Do not breastfeed for about a week after the dose
This does not protect against sexually transmitted infections
Seek care for severe lower abdominal pain (rule out ectopic pregnancy)
pk: Delays ovulation within hours; contraceptive effect over the relevant fertile window
Single dose effective for the at-risk window (up to 120 h post-intercourse)
pearls: Two very different uses: a SINGLE 30 mg dose for emergency contraception (ella, FDA-approved) versus 5 mg daily for uterine fibroids (Esmya, EU only - NOT FDA-approved and now restricted due to rare serious liver injury).
Ulipristal is effective up to 120 hours (5 days) after intercourse and retains efficacy late in that window better than levonorgestrel.
Do not give with levonorgestrel or start progestin contraception immediately - progestins can blunt ulipristal's ability to delay ovulation; wait 5 days then use a barrier method.
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, certain antiepileptics, St. John's Wort) reduce efficacy.
missed: Emergency contraception is a single dose, so there is no 'missed dose'; take it as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse. If vomiting occurs within 3 hours, repeat the dose. (For the EU fibroid 5 mg daily regimen, take a missed dose when remembered unless near the next dose.)
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited; no specific antidote. Single doses up to 200 mg have been tolerated without serious adverse effects. Manage supportively.
